While the music itself is nice as a background for events, there's also location-specific BGM which is simply playing when you're at one of the locations on the island. This music is just BGM, it doesn't follow any direciton. However, there are very few silent moments in the game; almost always somebody is talking, and as a result this BGM is very often
unfitting. It's also sometimes a bit too loud, and there's no option to turn it off or reduce its volume. There are plenty of places in the game which would feel much better without any music at all, just background sounds.
It's intriguing but I can't call it especially profound or anything. Ultimately it's just a mystery story. Not much emotional or psychological conundrum there, to be honest.
Voice acting is pretty solid and the characters are fleshed-out, so you probably won't be bored.
Since it's a dialogue-based game, it's practically nonexistent. There are some collectibles though, and looking for them is really boring considering how slowly the characters move around the world. The radio thing is a nice touch, but it's nothing we haven't seen before.

Spoiler Free Review:
Come on, how can there be spoilers for game that is almost two decades old….
Nostalgia is a powerful force, and this game brings it back full throttle.  Age of Empires 2 has a cult following for sure, it was a masterpiece at its time – everyone played it, I’m not going to delve into that so much as a comparison to the HD version, and if it is worth playing now.
Let’s start with the HD – there is nothing HD about this.  Graphics may be polished, but it is nothing compared to AOE3 or StarCraft, or any other comparable RTS – the game still shows its age.  The AI has been improved from what I remember of the original, and several times in the single player campaigns I had to restart because I wasn’t fast enough and the AI has me in a corner.  The gameplay challenges have been welcomed and aren’t frustrating.
The issues that plagued the original are still present, troop movement being one.  You have to carefully monitor your army and not send them across the map in one move.  AI movement still causes troops to get separated from the pack, or take a pretty stupid route.  The rock paper scissors mechanics are still in effect (send pikemen to horses -  swordsmen to pikemen – etc).
Some other changes that the HD version brings include map size, population limit increase, and where this game is really shining – new civilizations.  The new expansions include civilizations and single player campaigns that equal the original.  They did a fantastic job of keeping the feel of the original, but adding in the different content that sets it apart.  In the mind of this reviewer, the DLCs are totally worth it.  The population increase has also been welcomed.  I tend to turtle during single player games and being able to open the gates of Mordor and flood the map is very satisfying.
AOE2 at the time was the number 1 game out and became a classic.  Fan outcry brought it back full force, and I have to say it is just as enjoyable as I remember.  How much of that is nostalgia and how much is actual good game mechanics is up for debate, but I find myself pouring hours and hours back into a game, that is still around after almost 20 years.
Rating: 8 out of 10.  Highly Recommended.
Playing on i7-6700, 16Gb RAM, GTX1070

Originally smart phone games were littered with action RPG’s. They contain simple controls, simple to make and are great time sinks. Since then we’ve moved away from long sessions of gameplay too games which can be played while you drop your kids off at the pool. Hero Siege is an action RPG from smart phones and carries many of the same elements the original action RPGs had.
Hero Siege is class based with your usual archetypes while also containing quite a challenging and lengthy campaign. It has a progression system which is persistent through all playthroughs while still having mini perks you gain throughout the dungeons. The closest game that comes to mind would be The Binding of Isaac, where a majority of your power depends on what item pick-ups you get throughout your travels.
The items vary from flying fedoras shooting pi symbols (3.14159), angel wings and even the ever so popular Frostmourne from World of Warcraft. While the pop culture references may be nice they also have vastly different effects. This brings the most replay value to the game as you can get any number of item combinations which causes much hilarity.
This also causes major balance issues though, as these items only last one playthrough and this can cause a large gap in difficulty depending on the items you acquire. Luckily there are persistent elements which keep things from going to crazy. Also the class specific abilities can sometimes cover your short comings.
The port is kind of a mess, 4:3 aspect ratios at max res of 940x640, the sound options are on and off and only for music, there are no re-bindable keys and I experiences a handful of crashes(stability has been improved in some updates)
While it has its issues it delivers on what it promises, an action RPG which will have you playing for hours while you get mad over what loot you get. It has enough content for the price but the quality of content can be debated between person to person. Personally I enjoyed my time with Hero Siege and with some of the recent updates it’s only looking better.
As Long as they add more textures to outside walls and more options for in home items its an all around fun 3D Designer, Great Work!

(quick note: I played this game off Steam for many, many hours. I know what I'm talking about!)
Dark Messiah is a really interesting case of a game being completely carried by a single gameplay element.
In most respects, this game is unremarkable. It takes place in the Might and Magic universe, but bears almost no resemblance to its namesake. In fact, the only thing "M&M" about this game is the villain being a member of the necromancer faction. If you took the word "necromancer" out of the script, it would just be another generic fantasy world. The story is extremely simplistic and transparently linear; the average dialogue will be "I am <name>. The <Macguffin> is at <location>. I will <plot>. Good luck!" Sometimes, the only thing pushing you forward at all is the knowledge that you're in a videogame and have an objective. As for the characters... Sareth, the protagonist, only speaks to complain or prompt other characters to provide exposition ("What is <Macguffin>?" or "I'm tired of staring at a horse's ears"), Xana is just a sultry tease-dispenser ("You did all of this for a hug. If I were there..."), Leah is the hopeful love interest ("With you here, we should have the <Macguffin> in no time!"), and every other character has too few lines to even be described. Combine this mediocrity with a scrabbled-together Source engine full of bugs and freezes and you get an overall disappointing experience. Well, except for one BIG thing...
The combat in this game is sublime. Attacks are directional, animations flow into each other seamlessly, combos feel satisfying, and the environment is RIFE with opportunities to punish your opponents, with plenty of blood and gibbing to reward you for the effort. There are three combat styles: melee, ranged, and magic, and each style has substyles (for example, melee has sword-and-board, staves, daggers, sneak attacks and backstabbing, and so on). Fighting in this game just feels good. There's one level in particular which gives you a compound full of easy-to-kill goblins and lets you wreak havoc however you wish. I won't lie, I love to reload that level and play it over... and over... and over... and over, trying out different methods for mass murder. Perhaps most satisfying is the synergy you can develop between styles. For example, you can shoot a blackguard in the leg from behind, then tear his head off while he's limping. However, the most iconic moment in this game is when you kick an enemy into a spiked wall or off of a cliff. Seriously; if you thought you already had the most satisfying kicking experience you could in a game, YOU THOUGHT WRONG. The kicking alone makes this game "good", and the rest of the combat bumps it up to "memorable".
Should you buy this game? Well, have you ever wanted to kick an orc into a pillar holding up the wall of the building, causing the wall to crash down and kill a dozen orcs and goblins before they can react? Have you ever wanted to beat a crowd of people to death using the dead body of one of their friends? Have you ever wanted to slit a foe's throat and kick their dying body off of a cliff above the clouds? Most importantly of all, have you ever wanted to beat an entire video game by just kicking people into stuff? If any of these sounded like fun, you should probably drop a couple bucks on this game.
P.S. The multiplayer is fun if you can get a couple people together for it. It's a real kickapalooza.

I never thought in a million years I would be playing a new Sonic game, much less this title.  I tried it out during the most recent sale because I was pretty bored and I was completely blown away.  Not only is it a very polished racing game, it's a great tribute to many years of Sega's past.  I love seeing some of the old characters come back to life that were mainly left behind in the 90s and 2000s.  The tracks are all unique and original.  Every character handles differently and more or less appropiately.  I have to say Sonic definitely feels underpowered in this game and I'm pretty happy with that.  The career mode is probably one of the most frustrating things about this game though, not the levels or the handling of the cars, or even the quirky A.I. no...it's the design of the career progression.  You earn stars (go figure).  These stars accumate in a pool and the more stars you unlock, the more becomes available to you.  Sounds pretty typical right?  Wrong.  Getting the latter stars is a pain-staking, eye-gouging, fist shaking, experience that will leave you cussing and throwing your controller.  Not only does the game get harder, it feels almost impossible at times.  You /have to finish/ first or beat the clock by some stupid amount of time or blah blah blah.  It doesn't really reward you very well for attempting nor does it give you a star or anything like that.  It's a all or nothing type deal.  You earn your freaking stars.  So, you get some of the content when you finish the game on "medium" but you'll be about eh...60+ stars short of getting most of the content.  Just saying.  It's a steep mountain from there.  I'm still missing around seven characters and a few tracks and this is my first play through.

Andoran Skye XD is a graphically outstanding game for being made by one man.
Sound wise it has great sound effects and music, being a pure text base game it makes up for the lack of voices with a great music selection i assume was made the creator himself. I noticed that very rarely that the sound effect from attacks will stop abruptly when another enemy is scripted/has its chance of attack.
Graphically the game is top notch when you look at some other games that have a team of a dozen working on it and it comes out being slightly inferior to this game, at no point did i actually not stop to look at the background or other characters for each one was unique even though they didnt add much or anything to the story they looked the part and made up for lack of helpfulness in humor.
As far as the Gameplay goes there are some hiccups and confusion in the game for example Chain Attacks are never explained through the course of the game even though when i did have a chance to try the mechanic out is proved to be very helpful on three of the bosses. Also some characters have skills out shined by ones they already have or later recieve
another example would be Catalina's attack Melody Mash over her Mint Powder, Chadricks series of Red Bashes or WarRab's Single target Attacks. Another thing to keep in mind when you do play the game is the Stat Growth of your character, Special attacks still seem to be able to put points into when they are maxed out, as i experimented with this to see if it actually did make them stronger or if it was just a bug i wasted a few levels on Catalina and WarRab (about two each) just to find out it did not infact make them stronger and if it did there was no noticable or worth damage up.
The Replay Value so far isn't there, i have been told that the game could go through several changes while being polished to give it some sort of end game, maybe some sort of dunegeon or something gamers always love, a NG+ to just faceroll the game that did you dirty the first go round.
All in all Andoran Skye XD is a great lesser known game to try out to support the creator for this wonderful game, once again the story is a great thing to atleast experiance and the gameplay although it has some hiccups i found personally addictive. I would definately reccomend this game to anyone looking for something cheap to play around with.

As someone who played the hell out of every single Mario Kart game, I was truly suprised by this game.
It makes alot right and is just pretty fun.
The graphics are really nice,
the controls are well done (I`m playing it with an Xbox 360 Controller),
and the gameplay is fair and challenging.
If you played one of the latest Mario Kart games, the controls of this game will feel really familiar.
The drifting and driving is pretty much the same. (Plus planes and boats - those stear "ok enough")
What I really like about this game: No rubberbanding!
It doesn`t matter if you are first or last : you always have the chance of collecting a good powerup.
And that is fine, because the most powerups require some skill to hit your target, and every homing weapon can  be evaded with skills.
There are enough tracks to never get bored in online multiplayer -  wich is alot of fun.
The online multiplayer goes pretty fast from race to race without wasting to much time in between.
vote a map, select your driver + car setup and the next race will begin.
Matchmaking does work well, there are always other players to find and online sessions are quite solid and lag free.
The singleplayer is also pretty well made.
It's not getting boring, since you have a tree shaped overworld with different challenges. Normal races, traffic attack, boss fights and other modes keep you amused while you unlock new drivers. And there are quite much of them!
You earn XP by racing and can unlock new setups for your race vehicle by leveling up. A nice touch!
Bottom line: I can't wait for Mario Kart 8, but Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed is much more than a fill-in.
It's the first true competition for Nintendo's kart racer that brings new ideas, is more skill-based than depending on item luck and will hopefully return.
This can just make both games better, and I`m sure Nintendo will learn some lessons from this game to make Mario Kart even better.

Arcane Studios second major release Dark Messiah of Might & Magic stands up to the test of time, by providing fast paced meele action with physics based gameplay elements.
After their hommage to the Ultima Series "Arx Fatalis" Arcane Studios created a still to this day unique game as part of Ubisofts relaunch of the equally iconic Might & Magic franchise. The game's story takes place a generation after the conclusion of the turn based Heroes of Might & Magic V. You are Sareth, a young wizard's apprentice, tasked with accompanying a expedition in search for an ancient artifact "The Skull of Shadows". The story is mostly a backdrop, but also doesn't get in the way of combat, for which you have the choice between very distinct playstyles:
- Charge into meele with heavy armor and supporting magic at your disposal?
- Use the Thief inspired stealth system to sneak and assassinate your enemies or sometimes even avoiding combat entirely?
- Be an archer, who can fall back on lethal daggers or fast swordplay in a tight spot?
- Lay traps to soften your enemies up to then uttely destroy them with elemental magic?
This marketed diversity of playstyle still holds true to this day. The great level design caters to most playstyles and offers a great amount of secrets and alternate ways to approach encounters.
All in all an amazing experience, which influence can still be witnessed in the melee system of their follow-up franchise Dishonored.
You buy this game for the puzzles and the deep story, but mostly for puzzles.

What is Andoran Skye XD, what did Chadwick Evans want to achieve with this game, honestly I have no clue because this game will make you rage quit too often because it is trying to be too many things all at once and failing every time.
It tries to be a mix of side scrolling RPG like Secret Of Monkey Island and button mashing fighting like Tekken and I say bravo to the idea. This could easy be a new level of game play that could bring hours of fun but some how turns you into slobbering demon of rage and spewing forth words from Barry Manilow’s greatest hits! (My wife had to leave the room! Yes, it was that bad).
The story behind Andoran Skye XD is a tale where an evil dude in a cloak Is looking for an artefact that helps control the world of Andoran (I think) We then cut to a young man called Chadwick who is minding his own business when an earth quake (or explosion, it is not clear) interrupts his reading in the library. In amongst the confusion Chadwick falls through the floor into a basement. He tries to find a way out and comes across a mysterious chest that contains a glowing stick or staff (again it is not truly clarified), that instantly zaps him to the lands of Andoran (or zaps him to another part of Andoran, I can’t say, a lot of the starting story is so unclear I fell like I’m reading mud!)
Upon waking Chadwick is greeted by Tredun, a man in a trench coat looking like he is ready to go all Blade Runner on Chad’s♥♥♥♥♥♥than be an actually a spell caster (which he is suppose to be). Tredun informs a bewildered Chadwick that he is the saviour of Andoran and needs to meet with a surviving Elder.  And here starts the adventure (Hell).
You move through the land using your WASD & QE keys, plus interact with items with your mouse.  A & D for moving left and right of screen, W is to jump and Q and E to cycle left of right of a given path when a path choice arrow pops up on screen (no character movement for S but crouch would have been nice).
Here the first sign of problems with this game is the ‘Path choice’, no matter how many times you try to cycle to a different path, the game will have none of it and automaticlly kicks you to a predetermined path, so there really is no freedom of choice (The Chad giveth and the Chad taketh away).
The next flawed gem is the fighting sequences. The first two tutorial bouts are a farst, fighting is in real time so you do not get a chance to plan you attack or defence. The tutorial points out that you use certain keys to use but no key is given accept a [Choose] or [Cancel] is shown through out leaving you to push buttons till you find a result (but not the one you need to find though). You also need to choose who is attacking and this requires you to click on which character you want to do the attacking then bring up a menu of their attacks. This is all well and good as the monsters attacking you in the first two tutorials just stand there like stunned mullets.
You move on to your third battle and you soon discover to you dismay that while fighting you need to mash a three key sequence of buttons to block an attacking monster’s attack (either WASD). No where is this mentioned in the first two and it is not a set sequence like in most fighting games but a random set each time the monster attacks. So you are virtually playing ‘Simon Says’ with your character’s blocks but you only have a split second to do the sequence.
During fighting a recharge button also pops up above a character’s head, so once they have done an attack you can not use them again till this bar is full (again this is not mentioned in the tutorial fights). You will also discover (by accident) that Q & E will bring up a wheel with Chain, Battle or Flee written on it. Battle is obvious, Chain means that you can chain the power of both characters into an attack of the first person in the chain (which ever direction you choose to do the chain).  Again it is never clear if you are chaining power, stamina or strength, as the chain still has the effect of a single person. Plus once used, everyone in your team will have empty bars so you are open to enemy attacks galore.
And with Flee, you can flee but you need to do a three key sequence to achieve the right to flee.
The third battle is easy enough that you can either win or run away but when you come to leave the jungle you are faced with your forth battle and the reason why you may rage quit.
Your forth battle is with a Lion type creature who has a mother load of health and some heavy handed attacks. You will die quickly if you can not master the blocking key sequence..
Oh and did I forget to mention that the key sequence for blocking or Fleeing, is now any random combination of between three to ten key strokes that must be done in a blink on an eye. And trying to bounce between which of your two characters has enough fight bar filled to make an attack, via the mouse, just leaves you open to a world of hurt as it only takes two hits from Mr Lion to see you flop to the ground dead.
I have still yet to pass this battle after several hours of trying, crying and quit rage. Even my lap top has put out a Domestic Violence Order against me because of this (Please laptop, let me play, I promise not to hit you in the screen again, ok yes and no more thumping your keyboard. HEY! I only through you once across the room! The second time was an accident!).
Saving your game is at points marked by a pillar with an orb, but there is only one before you first real battle.
Graphics is a mix of 3D environment and 2D characters, which works but leaves you felling that it is a little tardy. You can choose resolution and whether you want full screen or windowed in options.
Music is good but nothing to write home about but you can turn it down in options (Yaaay!), the bar for volume though is a flame and you need to guess where up and down is for volume.
A final flaw to this game is when you exit, twice on me the game has effected Steam, I have not been able to use my mouse other than to scroll up and down. Even shutting and restarting Steam will not fix it. Only through restarting your computer will Steam function properly, so be wary of this.
I am hesitant to call this a review, on the clear fact that I can not break through the forth battle and progress with the game. A better player may push through and find this a rather good game, and I will state that the idea of combining an RPG adventure with a Tekken type battle engine was sound but it fells poorly implemented.
Anyhow, I have awash this game from my memoirs and am now going on a round the world trip with my laptop, to patch up our grievances and rekindle our love for one another. Bon Voyage.

NaissanceE is a walking simulator with jump and run elements and... let´s say an interesting "Story".
I´m going to try to "describe" the game and the Story (believe it or not, no Spoilers).
Also the Screenshots tell you exactly what you get :P
Gameplay:
It took me around 3 hours to "complete" the Game.
A lot of Walking, running and Jumping, with a few Jump and run sections.
The movement feels responsive and direct.
Even tho there is a Health system (Regeneration over time), there are no enemies which could make use of that.
There are no unlockables, no achivements or something like that.
World:
The entire world is gigantic and gives off an omnious and mysterious feeling with a fitting soundtrack. It looks impressive.
The entire World is abstract and made with geometrical shapes and bodys. There aren´t any plants, birds or something like that, only you and the world with it´s few entites (It´s unknown, if they are living beings or machines)
Almost no Color is used in the entire game, 85% of the game you´ll only see White and Black and good lighting effects.
The Levels have no obvious linear path, which means, the World looks and feels enormous but you can easily get lost (at least at the start of the game)
Story:
The Game starts with a cutscene (the ONLY cutscene in the game), showing the protagonist running through a hallway running away from something and falling in a hole, that´s it. There isn´t a single word written or spoken in the entire game (Except the title of the Chapters).
The game abruptly ends (It´s sudden, but you don´t get the that "What? That´s it?" feeling) with an open end. No questions will be answered by the game when you finish it ( ;_; ).
How in the description written, you create your own story in your head while playing the game and discovering the fascinating world underlined by the great choice of music, which means, Imagination is KEY.
If you´d play the game, i suggest you play it in a dark room with complete silence and nothing to interrupt you while playing and taking your time exploring the world.
All in all, it´s Special and there are only few games, which capture the feeling of Size, emptiness (and loneliness) and mysteriousness that well like this game does.
Even tho it IS a bit pricey, get it on a Sale if you´re interested ;P

I was skeptical purchasing this game as I have very little experience in the Borderlands universe.  Turns out no previous experience was needed and WOW was I in for a suprise.
An excellent first chapter for a great new game.  If you are a tell tale fan you are in for a treat.  A fast paced and incredibly fun adventure. While it is a different direction for TellTale to utilize comedy rather than the darker elements in their other games, they pull it off so well with Tales from the Borderlands.  Making choices becomes fun and often times hilarious rather than intense and difficult.  You are less worried about who will die from your choices athen previous games and it allows you to get swept away.
Overall I HIGHLY recommend this chapter to anyone who loves TellTale games or really to anyone who loves a great story.  As much as I enjoyed the new Game of Thrones TellTale Game, I  am seriously anticipating the next Episode of Tales From the Borderlands, a little bit more!

Rimworld is an amazing game.
The game is a survival sandbox game that tells a story through its deep and complex features.
My best story is that of a hunter, who was horribly disfigured and couldn't do much except to hunt and tame animals.
One day while he was out hunting, a pack of wargs ambushed him and tore out his entire right hand. I was devastated for him. Will he never hunt again and be resigned to a life of animal herding?
No, he decided to not be a victim, and use a short-range shotgun. He found moderate success and could hunt reasonably.
Eventually, I would get my hands on a prosthetic and bionic arm, which my top doctor installed on him successfully. With the enhancement, not only could he hunt again, he could hunt better thanks to improved stats given by the bionic arm.
Finally he would be the one that "won" the game.
The story only scratches the potential that the game offers. It is strongly recommended for people who like survival sandbox games.

Good lord, what an amazing game!
I'd seen this one go by on my steam now for a while, and I'm sure I must have looked at it at least 2-3 times, and every time I'm sure I must have taken one look at it and thought "RTS", or "tower defense" and clicked on to something else. Then last night I felt like I wanted to play a game but I couldn't decide what game to play, or even what genre, and so I went trauling through my Steam to see what it had for relatively cheap. Nothing really stood out to me but this one came up again and I noticed it had overwhelingly positive reviews, so I gave up and went to YouTube to see a let's play because I wanted to see what this was all about.
I wound up watching probably 3-4 hours of one by some guy doing a custom scenario where he started out with one person and nothing else because that felt like the kind of scenario that I'd like to play. I could've happily enjoyed that, but it was a recent let's play so that's all he'd played so far. That was enough to convince me to drop the cash on RimWorld, though, and something like 13-14 hours later I'm glad I did.
This is an amazing game, and I can't believe how much fun I'm having playing it. I could've gone my whole life with just those uninformed ideas about how since it's all just 2D graphics that it must not be much more than a tower defense or RTS type game, but I would've missed out on a pretty amazing experience. This game is just awesome. I had questioned how it could be what it looks like and be priced what it is, but no, you get your money's worth out of it.
Read some other reviews from people with hundreds of hours of game play if you want more of the nitty gritty about it, because there's a pretty good bit to it that I haven't begun to uncover yet at only 13 hours in, but let me just add in to that overwhelmingly positive review stuff with my hearty endorsement.
For me, I'm reminded of ARK: Survival Evolved in terms of building things, albeit in 2 dimensions instead of 3, and without dinosaurs, although there are some pretty big looking animals I've seen once or twice now. And I'm reminded a bit of This War Of Mine in terms of how emotionally invested I've become with my first few characters and their pets. I bought a pair of little dogs from a visiting trader passing through, and had only had them just barely long enough to train them up the first level, when a wolf wandered up near my camp, and, while a couple of pirates had come to raid my base right after a man eating Muffalo had come through and terrorized us for a few days and attacked it and knocked it out before I could get outside and rescue it, then proceeded to eat it at my front doorstep. Despite having just barely bought the dog, I was just absolutely heartbroken and furious at the wolf for coming up and trying to eat my dog. It made me a lot more protective of the dog my first character came with, even considering keeping him confined to my base from now on because I can't bear to lose another one.
Anyway, this game is a lot more than it probably looks like it is. I'm a convert for sure, and I'm gonna be coming back to this game a lot for quite a long time to come. <3

The sentry bots move randomly, which means, if you want to move, you find a good covered spot, and wait for ideal sentry positions. I don't find this a problem, as planning routes or listening to the story keeps me busy. However, you won't win if you charge through the rooms eating all the furniture.
Some buildings don't have sentriy bots which is a nice change of pace, as the sentry levels can be stressful, and you can lose a lot of health on them. As long as you keep an eye on the lasers it's easy to make it past these levels unscathed.
Hands down, this game is difficult. Since you're forced to destroy cover, levels become progressively harder. If you like a good challenge, try Not The Robots.

Definitely one of my favorite story-based games. The characters and plot are great and pretty flshed-out, for the most part. A bit slow, especially because there's a fair bit of back-tracking, but still overall a worthwhile experience.
PROS:
- Nice aesthetics; everything feels in place.
- With the exception of Nora, all the characters you encounter feel realistic and grounded; even Nora isn't bad, just bland.
- Some replayability with branching choices and character development.
- Unique dialogue system. Can't say I've seen another like it, with different options or, if you want long enough, you don't say anything at all.
CONS:
As a note, these cons are more nit-picking than anything, as none of these are in any way gamebreaking.
- Too expansive. With no fast travel and a decently complicated map, it can feel a little tiring to traverse the island.
- Not the best pacing; The last third of the game does feel a little rushed.
- Pricey. Average playthrough of Oxenfree is about 4-6 hours depending on dedication and intuiition. At $20, I feel this is a ltitle overpriced for the playtime.
In conclusuon, I would definitly recommend Oxenfree, but maybe wait until a sale.

Unlike many giving this a thumbs-down, I *did* finish the game.  (I don't connect to the internet every time I play a video game, okay?  So the time logged on here is not accurate.)
Neutral is my official, unofficial rating.  If you have higher standards for story-driven video games, then this review is for you.
Although it has its merits (the decisions actually DO matter and the sound design is great), I don't think I'd go out of my way to recommend this game to everyone.
To be a great walking-intensive story-driven game, I think it needs to be very strong in two ways:  world-building and character.
World-building.  Sure, we learn why the freaky things are happening, but we don’t often interact with the environment; I don't learn much at all about the actual characters' world, which would have been better; the environment doesn’t change very much (just a bit).  As a result, I didn't feel like this was a world I could step into.
In the beginning, it was quite immersive, thanks to the clever jokes of the characters and the creepy, swallow-you-whole sound design as befitting a creepy/mystery game.  But I felt pulled out by the constant zig-zagging paths we have to walk through, and the rocks we have to climb ever-so-slowly, among other things.  I feel like it may as well have been a straight line with some trees in the background, I interacted with it so little yet had to wind through it, all the same!  And, in this respect, there was not enough game for the price, in my opinion.  Take away all the time I spent tuning the radio dial, spinning wheels, and walking and climbing, and there isn’t much else to the game.  In this way, it felt short.  I know that they were riding on the “much else” being the characters, I know, but ……
The characters didn't cut it, for me.  I learned who they were, sure, but it was not through particularly good story-telling (and how tiny they are on the screen!  You are purely reliant on their words and not their actions.). They TOLD their characterization rather than SHOWED thanks to the confines of the game’s setting.   As I said before, the world we explore in the game is not the usual world of the characters, so we learn very little about the characters we interact with through the world.
The way the characters were written felt just plain off.  The devs’ primary focus seemed to be to make the characters churn out clever jokes and cavalier reactions of “Well…..  That was super weird, right?” like they were in a campy movie.  However, in all other respects, this game is not campy; the main story line took itself quite serious.  So why were the characters being so self-aware?  Shouldn’t how they react to these horrors reveal who they are as individuals and not as a wink to the audience?
Also, something that surprised me: it made my laptop burn up like crazy!  This game didn't look that graphically demanding.....
I recommend you play this game instead:  Night in the Woods.  It could be called a "walking simulator," but it doesn't feel that way!  It has great world-building and wonderful characters.

I expected a different game when I first started playing Hero Siege. Here I was thinking it was an action RPG, you know, with quests and loot, but I guess it was the name that fooled me. Hero Siege is actually a fun, difficult but very, very addicting game that mixes RPG mechanics together with roguelike gameplay.
The game generates a random level for you, even though all of the levels are always large rectangles with randomly placed objects in it.
The enemies will come from the north, south, east and west and they come in waves. Defeat a wave and you'll have time to upgrade your stats and skills, find health orbs, find hidden dungeons or buy items. Or just idle, it's totally up to you. You can also find and unlock chests for more money and random items. And there are potions to be found as well, but they can have a negative effect as well as a positive effect. Same goes for shrines. In other words, there's plenty to be found in these, seemlingly small, levels.
After every fifth wave comes a boss fight, but because you'll have properly upgraded stats and items by then they're usually a piece of cake. Defeat the boss and you're awarded money and/or chests, a random item (these items are very similar to the ones found in The Binding Of Isaac) and a portal. Enter the portal and you'll enter the next area, with full health, and the game continues again, except with more and more difficult enemies this time around.
And after many, many waves you'll enter a new world. If you die you can start from there, but it's more difficult right from the start and you won't have any of your previously gathered items this time. Still, it can be done with a little practice.That's pretty much what Hero Siege is all about.
The graphics aren't great; they're pixelated, especially in full screen and things can get a bit hectic with all the stuff that's going on but it's definitely better than 3D graphics. They just wouldn't fit the game. There's no voice acting except for a few phrases and the sounds consist mostly of little soundbites. But that's not what's important here. The fact is that Hero Siege is a fabulous game that you desperately need to play. Trust me.

During the game's intro, it declares that it will cause people to 'rage again'. I thought it was a reference to difficult games, that are great, but can be frustrating at times, such as Super Meat Boy. This was probably the dev's intention, however, this was not why I raged!
Simply put this a 2d platformer, and it seems there are a plethora of these going around at the moment. The genre is going through something of a revival, and there are loads of really cheap, and excellent games of this type thanks to indie developers.
So why is this game so utterly bad?
First off, there does not seem to be any controller support. In a game of this type, that is always going to be a major issue for me. So then I went into the options menu to try and learn the keys. Nope, there was no way to learn the basic controls, let alone change them! At this point I could see many red flags, before the eventual red mist.
Next, the game starts. Graphics were poor, really basic, and uninspired. It made some genuine 8-bit games of old look pretty! Music was repetitive and very grating. Yet another factor to add to the overall miserable experience of this disastrous title.
Then the ultimate kick in the balls. The gameplay...or sheer lack of it! Platformers of all ilk, live and die (no pun intended) due to their gameplay. A 'hard-as-nails' game, as this pupports to be, can be excused if it has fine gameplay, and the player knows that they died due to their mistake. It's what creates a kind of zen moment in platform games, when you zip along, with only your reflexes and guile to keep you going. Well, with atrocious level-design. clunky movement, and glitchy enemies, there is no gameplay whatsoever.
Listen I know this game is cheap. That does not mean you should buy it. In fact I think the dev should pay us all for the mental anguish that this steaming pile inflicts on the gamer!

But I do have this tiramisu recipe I saved
6 large egg yolks
3/4 cup sugar
3/4 cup whole milk
Four 8-ounce containers mascarpone cheese, at room temperature
1 1/2 cups espresso or strong coffee, at room temperature
1/2 cup brandy or cognac
30 to 32 crisp Italian ladyfingers (savoiardi)
1/4 cup Dutch-process cocoa powder
Bittersweet chocolate, for shaving
Line an 8-inch-square baking dish with plastic wrap, leaving a 3-inch overhang on all sides. Fill a large bowl with ice water. Make the custard: Whisk the egg yolks and sugar in a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of barely simmering water (do not let the bowl touch the water) until the sugar dissolves. Slowly whisk in the milk and cook, whisking constantly, until the custard is light and foamy, about 10 minutes (a thermometer inserted into the mixture should register 170 degrees F). Remove the bowl from the saucepan and set in the bowl of ice water; whisk until the custard is cool, about 1 minute. Put the mascarpone in a large bowl. Fold the custard into the mascarpone with a rubber spatula until almost combined, then whisk until just smooth (do not overmix or the custard will be grainy). Combine the espresso and brandy in a shallow bowl. One at a time, dip the ladyfingers in the espresso mixture until soaked but not soggy; arrange 2 rows of about 5 biscuits each in the baking dish. Spread one-third of the mascarpone custard over the ladyfingers. Repeat with a second layer of espresso-dipped ladyfingers, arranging them in the opposite direction. Top with another one-third of the custard. Repeat with the remaining ladyfingers, alternating directions. Spread the remaining custard on top and dust with the cocoa powder. Cover with plastic wrap; refrigerate at least 4 hours, or overnight. Invert a plate on top of the tiramisu, then flip the tiramisu with the plate. Remove the baking dish and plastic wrap. Invert a serving plate on top of the tiramisu and flip again so it is cocoa-side up. Remove the remaining plastic wrap. Shave curls of chocolate on top with a vegetable peeler.

NassinceE is an experience. An experience of anxiety, isolation, bewilderness and amazement. It is also an explorational adventure in a beautifully built up abstract world. The world is a perfect blend of magical realism, sci-fi horror and the staircase scene from labyrinth. Although the game is linear it will keep on popping up surprises and little twists until the very end.
You are alone -mostly- but the sense of tension and being haunted is always there. The architecture, the lighting, the music, the sounds, the fitting awkwardness of the level design at times. Everything sucks you in and you won't get out until about four hours later, depending on how much time you spend gaping around at how awesome the scenery looks. Just look at the screenshots to define if it's your style or not, it was totally up my ally anyway.
There's not just walking and staring, there are some not too difficult puzzle sections and some mildly annoying platforming sections. Some of them held me back a little bit too long, but they are far from impossible. Also I don't really understand why the breathing mechanism was there at all. You can run, but you have to press the mousebutton every four seconds or so to keep running. I guess it's supposed to add up to a sense of anxiety and vulnerability, but it got annoying pretty soon as far as I'm concerned. But nothing gamebreaking, it might work out for you.
If you're like me and love creative artsy gaming worlds in a first person walking simulator style this is a must play, no need to hesitate (I did, I don't know why). NaissanceE left a great impression on me and I am happy to have experienced it. Just don't play it when you're epileptic, suffering from migraines or if you're on a very bad trip.

Shigeru Miyamoto once was asked the secret of how he made Super Mario Bros. so great. He said, "When your game is about jumping, you make sure the basic act of jumping feels great."
Naissance is a walking simulator. And I **love** Walking Simulators. Gone Home, Firewatch, all the minimal-input Telltale Games you can find - sign me up! But they failed to learn the lesson Miyamoto was teaching.
You're dumped into a dark hallway after a spooky techno-smoke-monster makes you fall. OK, this is great. I can work with this. Then you do a little traversal following a glowing orb. Alright, that's a fine tutorial, we're 10 minutes in, I'm on board. Then we get to "jumping in the dark."
Oh boy. Does this game ever go off the rails once you have to navigate first-person jumping puzzles with an anemic midget apparently unable to clear, climb or navigate anything. Just moving around feels miserable, glacial, and boring. Then you miss a jump. So now you get to do EVERYTHING over again. Once you make it to the end of a hallway that requires you either
a) guess you need to turn left, duck, walk straight for
, then turn right to see your glowing floating breadcrumb and walk into the next room
or b) turn your Gamma up to 4 so you can see what the hell is going on
Oh, and the next room has a light-pulse that is literally blinding (like a flashbang that lasts five+ seconds) that you need to hustle out of the room while the door (that you can't see because of the flashbang) is open.
Once you're out, you get a long hallway. At one end: nothing at all! At the other: a cryptic unclimbable puzzle that you're supposed to just walk around.
There's more climbing and jumping, all with impossible-to-see darkness or edge-obliterating light, none of it fun or interesting. Smoke monster shows up? Any sort of environmental world-building? NOPE. Just Na'vi taking some midnigh shifts at the world's worst Xen level manufacturing plant.
I hate hate hate hate hate this game. Do not play it.

NaissanceE is a psychedelic first person platformer with a minimalistic approach to visuals and story.
The simple visuals are certainly stylish but get rather repetitive and boring quickly. On a positive note this simple visual style allows massive open areas with tons of visible objects.
The sound effects are not particularly good and the breathing sound in particular is quite annoying. The sound track is even worse and the background music is often extremely annoying.
The gameplay in NaissanceE is pretty terrible. The level design may be visually impressive but makes the levels really annoying to actually play. Lot of the time you are just aimlessly wandering around, trying to work out what you are supposed to do next. There are few simple puzzles too, but none of them are particularly challenging or imaginative.
The game also uses a really annoying checkpoint system with lots of poorly placed checkpoints. This is even more tedious considering how much the game relies on deadly hazards and trial and error. The breathing mechanic is rather annoying too and doesn't serve any real purpose.
The game is really tedious but not very difficult. All the puzzles are simple and none of the platforming sections are that difficult.
The controls are passable although slightly unresponsive.
The game doesn't really have a proper story or writing for that matter.
The movement physics can be quite buggy and the game suffers from quite a few visuals glitches too.
NaissanceE is one of the most tedious games I have ever played. Despite the short length I almost gave up several times. I didn't like the game at all and wouldn't recommend it.

I am the furniture eater! Everything is edible, delectable garbage!
Welcome to a stealth furniture-eating simulator, where you, a sentient robotic garbage can, must eat as much furniture and appliances as you can without tripping the defenses of the office buildings. Okay, you don't HAVE to stealth, but if you want to get cut through by rotating lasers, slam your mechanical face into prototype Aperture Material Emancipation Grills, get chased by floating mines, and shot at by mobile sentry bots, then be my guest.
Not the Robots is a very fun and somewhat arcady game with procedurally-generated levels. As you go through the game, you'll unlock new powerups you can collect and use to defend yourself - but you will also unlock new tricks and traps to avoid, making the game more challenging as you progress. Each level starts you at an elevator, and you will need to eat enough furniture to satisfy your electronic stomach - along with completing various other objectives that you need to unlock the elevator and continue on to the next level. How much furniture you eat, how many levels you make it through, and how many bonus objectives you complete, will determine the amount of points once your run ends - whether that results from you somehow managing to get through all of the office buildings, or, more likely, meeting an untimely demise at the hands of office security. You might be able to collapse yourself and hide behind desks and computer monitors, or even slide under a table and then sprint away when no one's looking, or teleport away just before that mine comes around the corner, but be aware - the traps get more devisive, and the sentries get more tools up their sleeve, especially if they see you. So your best bet is to not get noticed in the first place.
This is quite an enjoyable game, and if you happen to get bored or want something different than the regular office building dynamic, there are also various challenges that unlock as you make progress through unlocking levels and achieving certain goals. Perhaps, you might even strive for finding out what the story is behind this whole mess - if you can find those computer logs scattered throughout the levels at random. It's good for sinking in a small twenty minutes, or taking an entire afternoon. It plays smoothly, sounds great, and its visuals have a very gritty yet childlike cartoon quality to them that makes it that much more enjoyable to roll around in.
Highly recommend it.

Not The Robots might've just created a new genre of video game: the skill based stealth game.
Let me explain, most stealth games have set enemy patrols and cover. You're encouraged to take your time and plan for the perfect path through the level. NTR has a section at the beginning of each level where you can attempt to make a strategy, but if you try to aproach this game the same way you approach other stealth games you will be severely punished.
Not only do the patrolling enemies not have set paths but, as soon as the first enemy spots you, the furniture (your only cover) begins to TELEPORT AROUND THE LEVEL. This can lead to some stupid moments where you're hiding in a one exit room behind the last peice of cover (which you've strategecly left behind after eathing the rest), then suddenly the cover is gone and you get killed by the 5 enemies that happen to be in the room at the moment. Most of the time, however, the mechanic serves as a way to force you to think on your feet. NTR shines the brightest at the moments where you run into a room, a small army of sentinals on your tail, and have to quicky find the best peice of cover in a room that was literaly thrown together randomly. In short, any amount of planning won't help you in NTR, you will be judged on your knowledge of the core game mechanics, fundemental knowledge of how line-of-sight works, and nothing more.
oh, and the "perfect advertisement" storyline clips are hallarious.

RimWorld is one of those games you could play every day for the rest of your life and have a completely different outcome each and every time. It's a library of books, each game a brand new cover. Will you build a ship and escape or succumb to the dangers and mishaps around you? Will the favorite character who has fantastic shooting and a friendly face get mauled by a megasloth? Nobody knows. There is no script, only a story to be written after.
Aside from all of that, completely independent of it, this game supports mods. As we see from games like Garry's mod, mods can make a game immortal. Already, even before the game is done, there is a fantastic modding community adding things that we can only hope will be added by the developers.
TL;DR - Imagine prison architect 3000 years in the future except it's not a prison, it's the entire world. Oh and it has about twice the features and complexity. Plus mods.

It's hard to make a puzzle game that lasts for several hours and keep it interesting.
But that's what the Talos Principle did.
You're placed into the world, and you're pretty much free to complete it how you want, with the only limitation being your puzzle solving skills.
I'm surprised in how they were able to make so many of the puzzles interesting to solve, and adding new mechanics bit by bit did help keep me engaged. There were a few misses, but that's not something to be bothered by.
Also, the little pieces of lore and story intrigued me more and more as I discovered the world, and it was quite satisfying once I figured out of what might've happened.
The DLC was less interesting for me, but that's due to how difficult it was compared to the main game. I'm sure puzzle buffs will love the DLC. I did find the story taking place, while a bit more upfront, to be a lot more fun and enjoyable than the main game.
Mod maps are also allowed, which allows for really cool concepts made by the players.
Definitely something to get for small and big puzzle buffs alike, and for people who like to discover the story, but not for anyone else, to be honest.

Summary:
First-person Nazi-killing simulator, but with also starring cast of friendlies, at least one or two whom you're likely to care about a bit, and a couple of hostiles you'll hate.  There's a fair bit of story in cutscenes.  The plot is fairly bizarre, but... well, it has to bizarre in order to explain how the Nazis would have killer robots in 1945 and portable direct energy weapons in 1960.  Don't expect a bibliography and meticulously researched footnotes sourcing the various events in the game.
This is a loud/lethal game.  This is not a game where you'll be able to stealth your way through, whether lethally or not.  While it'll often be possible and to your advantage to discreetly thin the crowd with a sneaky thrown knife or  suppressed pistol headshot, there are enemies that cannot be discreetly fought, and alerts that cannot be avoid.   This isn't a Deus Ex or Dishonored game, although I did enjoy using the aforementioned suppressed pistol as I enjoyed Mr. Jensen's lovely Zenith.
It's not the longest game; it took me 13 hours for the first completion, and that's playing not terribly well at points and dying more than I should (reverting back to checkpoints -- there are no manual saves here), and not maximizing the use of what I had available (e.g. rarely using grenades).  I didn't fanatically explore and find every collectible, though.
Unlike the original Wolfenstein 3D, there *is* some character progression beyond getting inventory  -- you unlock some advantages (perks) by hitting various milestones.   Shoot enough enemies in the head and you'll get more headshot damage; stealthily kill enough Nazi soldiers and their hounds, and you'll get quieter footsteps; that sort of thing.  There's no experience points or leveling up beyond that, and your inventory is reset at the start of every chapter (but you retain whatever weapon upgrades you've found, so they'll be applied when you pick up that weapon again in later chapters).
On AI... hm.  It'll make frequent use of cover, and they will tend to try to flank you and flush you out.  They'e capable of quickly spotting and accurately shooting at you through fire and smoke to the point that I don't believe it hinders them at all.  On the other hand, they have fairly limited peripheral vision exacerbated by not looking around, their hearing is pretty bad so it's generally easy to sneak up on enemies so long as they're not looking in your direction, and there's certain areas where you can heavily abuse right-hand advantage or vents.  Deus Ex: Human Revolution enemies could toss grenades into a vent if they knew you were there; this won't happen here.
Mechanically, gameplay:  It's a pretty standard FPS.  Most interaction with NPCs is by killing them before they kill you.  There's not much in the way of platforming or puzzle-solving.  There are no "escort the seemingly suicidal and very fragile NPC" missions, there's no crafting or base building.  Stay alert, move carefully, stab or shoot or explode almost everything that moves, while getting each mission objective item or what-not.  If you're looking at FPSes at all you should be fine with what you need to do.  There's one brief driving session but it's rather simple even for somebody like me that generally hates driving in practically every non-Mechwarrior video game ever.
Technically; no technical issues on my end, w/ a 6700K + 980M + W10 setup.  Used mouse and keyboard; it's what I'm used to, and it makes sense for headshots.  No obvious bugs encountered.
Overall, t'was a fairly brief game but I enjoyed it for what it was.

One thing that NaissancE excels at, and really its whole purpose as a game, is presenting the player with a landscape so daunting and alien that you are driven purely by awe and curiosity to see where the game will take you.  The game doesn't have a story, though this is clearly intentional as you are dropped in this world of clean, monolithic structures, completely thrown off guard by its scale and spectacle of unknowns.  Though, a mood of dread is established early on, as your character narrowly escapes from something inexplicable and perhaps dangerous at the start of the game.  What this does is add a layer of something sinister to your adventure, as you never quite know what the purpose of this place is, nor if you are safe.
This uneasy feeling is the true art of the game.  It's making the player feel like an insignificant outsider in a strange land, devoid of life and seemingly, purpose.  It drives you to learn more, and to see more, even though there's a feeling in the back of your head like you're treading places that you don't belong in.  This world was not made for you, nor meant for you, and you could be taking your last step at any second.  It's hard not to persevere however, and in that sense, the game succeeds in being memorable for its forbidden nature that drives you to seek out its obscure secrets.  Despite this strange place instilling unease in every fiber of your being, you won't want to stop until you've uncovered whatever this all leads to, and it makes for a truly compelling and tense experience that shouldn't be missed.

There is some DLC for it that I probably purchased at some ridiculous steam sale price but I've yet to even play it. A tell-tale sign that this game is just too medicore to recommend.
Save your time and money and stay away from "Bored"erlands.

Almost a great game.
Pro
-amazing set peices
-some great scripting/animations
-some good songs
-profile selection for multiple players
Con
-way too little direction for progression
-very little actually logic involved, just exploring
-exploring punished in places(one part actually closes the game)
-exploring punished by easy death
-incredible dark
-can't remap controller
-poorly implemented breathing system for running(sounds like lamaze class)
-inconsistent quality and difficulty of obstacles
-no textures(feels like a pre-alpha)
This is an indie game that you can really tell was designed and coded by one person.  What it does well it does very well, the set pieces are amazing at times, some of the scripting and animations are very nice, and the music is pretty good at time.  Unfortunately thats about it for the positives.  The game is badly in need of textures which it doesn't use.  You can call this artistic license but feels like playing a pre-alpha game.  The level designs look amazing at times but lack contextual clues to give the player direction for the majority of the game and other than two puzzles logic really doesn't come into play.  You look around until you find a way forward.  This combined with game being incredible dark and being designed with the strange choice of punishing platforms with easy fall death make exploring much less fun than it sounds.  The baffling choice of the breathing mechanic implementation also adds to the frustration of having to click in rhythm while sounding like a lamaze class during all this exploring and running around.  And there will be running, many of the obstacles to progression require running and platforming.  Combined with the inability(that I could find) to remap the controller, this running is an extremely artificial way to increase difficulty.
With an actual team(producer, artist. etc.) this game could have be fantastic, it really does have potential but as is I can't imagine paying the full price for the game.   While it's obvious the designer wanted to go with the old school difficult platformer, after playing it seems very apparent that a exploration/walking simulator is much more suited to its strengths.

This is the worst sudoku game I've ever played, and is vastly inferior to literally any random free mobile game on the App Store or Google Play.
Made on the free version of Unity (the one that forces you to see the "Made with Unity" logo) in what I can only assume was about 20 minutes of work, this game features no volume control for its one loud song, no sound effects, badly aliased pixelated clipart (presumably just an emoji zoomed in), and absolutely no feedback upon your actions.  It doesn't even let you click a fruit and then click multiple squares, you need to click the fruit each time before hitting the next square.  Also, there doesn't seem to be any "pencil mode" and no ability to erase any mistake, either, all of which are features of literally every single sudoku game I've ever played.
The game doesn't have any progression the way that Sudoku Quest has differently-shaped boards to play on, you just start with 4x4 grids and play them until you get bored about 3 minutes later.  I managed to unlock "all the achievements" in 7 minutes thanks to it just being "win 5 games in a row" on the easiest boards on the planet, and that INCLUDES having to restart once.
The game doesn't even bother to check to make sure there is only a single unique solution to the puzzle! I ran across at least three in the nine boards I played where I saw that there were at least two valid solutions to the board, and yet the game didn't give me the achievement when I'd put in a valid solution!  This game fails at the most basic aspects of puzzle-making!

Age of Empires 2 is in my opinion the best game ever made. It's a timeless classic that is still just as enjoyable today as the day it came out. In my opinion it is the best RTS game of all time and for that to still be true 10 years later, it is certianly worth full price.
However, this is the HD version so it is slightly different. Graphics are practically the same - which is ok for such a timeless game. However it doesn't quite live up to it's HD title. However, I came back for the game - not for anything new.
This HD version HDifys the gameplay rather than the graphics. It adds a new map size and increases the highest pop cap to 500 - allowing for much better games if your PC can handle it. The new map size hurts the PC more than the pop cap though and I've played 500 pop games on a laptop on the old standard map size. I don't recommend doing that with more than one player though. Nonetheless, huge armies are very fun to play with and add that little thing that we probably would've modded in. However - if this is what sold you then make sure you have a decent PC for it because it gets unbearably laggy on certian systems.
Another update is the new AI which they patched in at some point. As a man who prefers to do single player, this new AI added a proper challenge to the old game when I played all the time during my childhood. I used to be able to take on 6 other AIs on the hardest difficulty all on the same team. Now I struggle against them on equal footing. However, you do have the option of playing against the original AI if you want. Even a mix if you really want. The only problem I've found with it is that it will focus on water whenever there's a significant amount of water on the map. This can be good at times but when they attempt a galley rush on highland and you walk right around them it's limitations can be quite apparent.
One big flaw is it's multiplayer. They've removed the LAN function for some reason. Despite this I still play this at LAN parties but we play through the online mode. A little bit annoying. Another thing is the lag. There's a noticable lag between when you click somthing and when it notices. This did cause problems but they are working on patching these problems out. The lag still exists but I'm no longer having the problem of me putting many houses in a line and it registering the house I accidently placed rather than the ones I wanted. However, I have played an entire game which was full of unbearable lag. However, it has multiplayer (the original's doesn't work anymore) and it actually lets you try the new civillisations from the expansion packs in it.
Overall, this is still the Age of Empires 2 that I loved all my life. It didn't need updating but they gave it a go and basically refreshed the experience a bit by letting me play on larger maps and with larger populations. Still the same game and therefor worth full price in my opinion. I'd personally say that the fact that the game is still being updated and you've got expansion packs if you want more, it's somthing you should get. Even if you've never played it you should try this game as it is the best game of all time in my opinion.

Summary - Squad is a modern tactical FPS, with large scale battles that are up to  50 v 50. Squad makes you focus on teamwork rather than solo play, It's different from other mainstream shooters and more like Arma and Insurgency. The game focuses on teamwork what happens through communication between the squad leaders, who are actually nice people. The first thing I enjoyed was in the game was the sound, this game, is possibly one of the best sounding games I've ever heard. Once you head in to a game for the first time you choose between squads once you're in a game, you will find that it being a tactical game and all, it has very slow gameplay as it mainly focuses on realism rather than arcade like other FPS games out there.
Pros
-Great sound the atmosphere in this game is truly astonishing, it actually feels like you're in the battlefield itself, gun sounds and explosions sound great.
-Good player base, squadleaders are for the most part are nice and take the game serious.
-Massive battles, Maps and the 50 v 50 gameplay is very immersive, feels amazing.
-Very Relistic, these types of games are not for everybody if you prefere fast paced combat this is certainly not the game for you, this focuses on the reality of modern warfare, without the emotion that is, your friend isn't really dead.
-Acually gets teamwork right for once, players follow commands and the game works better if you communite with each other and stuff actually gets done on the battlefield not like every other game were it's just like a bunch of people running around like savages.
Cons
-Graphics could be better, some aspects such a the sun's reflection is mesmerizing but overall the graphics ain't that good.
-It's too expensive knowing the amount of content, the amount of guns and gamemodes and so on, don't make a game that costs in this price range.
-No Rank up system, not everybody wants such a thing, it's more of a personal preference.
-I know it's still in Early Access but, some of the game is far from finished, such as the animations and some basic things. Mechanics such as vaulting have not been added yet, and they are still yet to be a huge variety of maps and vehicles.
-Lack of gamemodes, mabye it would be a good idea to possibly add in a few gamemodes, just an idea.
Verdict: Overall, SQUAD is one of the best tactical shooters I have ever bought, the non-arcade gameplay will put some people off buying it, if you like slow gameplay realism, tactical gameplay mixed in with a modern military, this is the game for you, I would recommend this game a lot for people who like these types of games, but for others people that like fast paced arcade shooters, won't really find this too appealing to them. Overall it's a great game and would recommend it

Lemme paint a little picture:
I was elected squad leader. It was my first time so i didn't want to disappoint. My squad spawns in on me and i see the majority of our team was heading up main street, fighting on the first contested point head-on.
The squad and i decide to swing wide the the west to a small house and set a rally point so we could have a safe hold out if the main firefight needs a point to fall back on. I'm dumb and have no idea how to commender a vehicle, so we go on foot.
Since we swung so far, we didn't see a single friend or foe, but heard the gunfire and explosions in the far distance. As we walk, we talk about interests, how we liked the game (it was a free weekend) and making semi-racist jokes about terrorists and poor countries.
One squadmate was bragging about how he had so many grenades for our team (the turban wearing team). Morale was high.
We get to the house, set up the rally and get bored instantly. We suit up once again and have the idea that we take the next town so when we do take the contested area, we will already control the next. But to do that, we would have to cross the gigantic field of what we assumed was wheat, out in the open. A good sniper could pick us off easily.
We circle up and brief my team. "Heads down, go fast, and if i saw drop, you drop." We start our sprint acoss the field, single file and looking for any sudden movements.
We make it to the back of the building we were aiming for. We circle up again and brief again, with a couple more jokes and such. Turns out, it was a small village, other side of this building was the main street that connected all the capture points together.
I heard a voice on the squad leader chat comms, there is an american humvee with a heavy machine gun on top in the point that the rest of the team was fighting, about 2 miles away. For a moment i thought the point he called out was our point, so i warned the squad.
After getting it clarified, and with a sigh of relief, we slowly start our way down the road toward the capture point.
I peek around the first corner down the road for about 30 seconds, making sure my squad has safe passage. Nothing. We again, single file, walked along the front of the building, being very cautious.
Once about three of us get on the front of the building, we start to hear some rumbling down the road in front of us.
"Oh S***! It's the humvee!! (squadmate i can't remember the name of) Get those grenades ready!! Fall back!"
We start sprinting as fast as we can to get behind the building again, as the humvee is just barreling down the road at high speed. Just before i get around the corner, the humvee opens fire and i get hit in the back.
I fall and it turns black. In th blackness, i hear my squad.
"Grenades going out!" accompanied by deafening gunfire where i could hear my squad screaming but couldn't make out the words.
I hear an explosion, and i could make out one squad mate say "I got you, but as soon as you get up, you gotta run back."
I get picked back up, i run my buns as fast as i can and follow the medic. I get behind the building once again, the two medics were there and a couple injured mates, among one of them, the guys bragging about the grenades. i ask him how he did.
"I threw all of my grenades and killed that humvee, but before that, a couple jumped out and held up across the street."
I peek around the corner along the side of the building to see two mates still firing across the road. Next to them in the ditch, a flaming humvee with black smoke billowing up that you could see from miles around. I was very proud.
I walked along the wall one more time to see the situation across the street, we had them surpressed well enough, i could see where they're hiding.
I tell them to stop firing and devise a plan, mixed with supressing fire and a smoke grenade, we flank around the side and about 3 minutes more of VERY cautious approach, we get all three of them. With heads held up high, we head to the capture point.
Our team takes the point behind us, we take the next point soon after that. And they run out of tickets and we win.
I congratulate my squad and tell them they were the best team a guy could ask for. I log out and never see them again...

Borderlands is set on the distant planet of Pandora - a Mad-Maxian desert like planet riddled with gang wars and strange alien beasts.
It's been some time since I've played Borderlands so my memory of this game might be lacking in some areas. To start this off, I'm going to say that I'm actually recommending against Borderlands. While this game does have good reviews there are a lot of problems with this game that keep me from personally recommending it.
Borderlands is what I'd describe as proverbial empty calories of gaming. Borderlands will keep you playing and you won't think that while playing a game that it's bad. This game is shamefully easy but rewards the player copiously with loot drops that keep the player interested. There's so much loot that even a packrat completionist gamer like myself was forced to ignore much of it.
After completing Borderland and experiencing its incredibly unsatisfying ending I felt it was a gross misuse of my time that ultimately left me unsatisfied as a gamer. Like a pint of Ben and Jerry's, Borderlands will keep you playing until the end but ultimately leave you with a feeling of shame.
There is some DLC for it that I probably purchased at some ridiculous steam sale price but I've yet to even play it. A tell-tale sign that this game is just too medicore to recommend.
Save your time and money and stay away from "Bored"erlands.

This game has a lot of content, it would be cool if the base game itself didn't suck.
There are two kinds of levels; levels with guards and levels without.
Levels without guards are easy, pointless, a waste of time.
Levels with guards though are very luck based. If a guard sees you, it will shoot you immedietly, no warning, and then stay in an enraged mode for the rest of the level, when in this mode they will shoot on sight, and vaporise cover, which will only respawn after a minute or so. Judging that you have to eat that cover to finish the level, it feels like a waste of time. You think the guards would go and investigate where you are? No actually, they just go around depending on where RNG (random number generation) takes them! Think you have a good plan, like in any other good stealth game, like Mark of the NInja, or invisible inc? Too bad, because theres a 90% chance that the guard will just turn around at some random moment or vaporise some cover your using. If the plan does work, your probably waiting three or four minutes untill it can work. The whole game just takes a long time, from waiting for guards to be in the right place, to waiting for cover that you have to eat to clear the level to respawn. There is an ability that makes it so you are invisible forever untill you start moving. Forever! This game is like rolling a dice untill you get two sixes in a row, then you can make a move and finish the level.
I think that the game would get better if the community wanted the devs to make it, they already added lots of game content that would fit nicely with an actually good game, but the game is dead, and the last update was around 2014, and when I write this review its 2016. The game is dead, and the devs couldn't even make it better before giving up and trashing it. Nice job devs, you have loads of extra content and challenges for a game that isn't even enjoyable.

NaissanceE is a 1st person puzzle + jumping platformer game with a little resemblance Antichamber and maybe even Minecraft. It has extremely minimalistic graphics style, a lot of running, some frustrating physics-based puzzles, no story and an overall feeling of madness.
The good:
- the graphics are stylish. They show how you can make an interesting and even pretentiously looking game by only using geometric primitives (mostly boxes) and only gray color (very rarely with some slight variations of gray). The game has a unique and definitive graphics style
- much of the visual greatness and even a few puzzles are built around the play of light. Overall there isn't much light in most levels, and the realistic light sources (white boxes) are scrace
- vast levels, especially the city-like level where you go down. I wonder how even Unreal engine could render such a huge number of objects. Maybe the fact that they are just boxes and are all gray helped? Still, they seem to use realistic lighting
- music is mostly good, sometimes even great, though I didn't like a few tracks (e.g. the last boss chase is annoying in its own, but the music makes it almost unbearable)
The so-so:
- there just isn't much you can do in the game. I wonder if the "use" key is actually ever used. You mostly run around, sometimes press buttons by stepping on them or running at them, or touch a light sphere to make it show the way. Also you jump and sprint (with a breath system which could as well be left out because it doesn't add anything and ends ups up being just a useless chore). Still, the scarcity of actions doesn't spoil the game, it just makes the puzzles somewhat limited
- the game lacks a sense of purpose or at least meaning. You solve a puzzle and don't get any reward or even a feeling of accomplishment - you just run forward to find another puzzle. There is a slight gratification in seeing vast new spaces for the first time, or simply moving on to the next area - but since no story connects the levels, the game feels arbitrary.
The bad:
- the jumping physics is somewhat clunky: you sometimes can't jump up on boxes in front of you. This also makes the sludges puzzle unnecessarily difficult because your character's collisions and jumps inside the sludge are pretty random
- there seems to be a bug that when running in a wind, you sometimes lose touch with the ground when pressing the sprint key, and you can't move any more. If you jump, you get instantly flown away and killed. This bug makes the level with tubes and ventilators extrememly frustrating, because you have to restart and retry sections many time until this bug doesn't happen and you can complete a section.
- a lot of running, and in a few cases the correct way forward is hidden in a huge area - you may spend 15 minutes just running around, wondering what's needed from you, only to find out that a tiny stars is hidden behind a ramp somewhere. The game just artificially lengthens your playtime by making you run around a lot. I thought it took me 8-10 hours to beat the game but, judging from Steam stats, it's just 5 hours.
Overall, it's a good game, and during the first 2 levels I wanted to give it a 9/10, especially after seeing the masterpiece 2nd level. However, the bugs in physics and the frustrating puzzles based on it, and the super-annoying final level make me reduce the rating to 8/10. It's still a very good game though, so if you're into indie game, don't get scared by its dull screenshots and give it a try.
