This game is good. Suprisingly good. It takes Diddy Kong Racing's multiple vehicle system, combines it with the customability of Mario Kart 7, and throws in all the lovely music and levels you should expect from any Sonic game.
You should consider making this your go-to party racing game rather than Mario Kart. The weapons are simple, yet well balanced. The rocket, ice, and blowfish all are nice to shoot forwards and backwards, but each have their own little niche to avoiding or dodging. Even this game's version of the "blue shell" is avoidable, assuming you have the skills to weave around it without hitting something else.
This game also has drifiting and tricks, which when mastered add some speed to your character, but will punish you harshly if you screw it up and get greedy (by either drifting too far or adding in one too many flips) There's no snaking here, but mastering the drifts and the flips really helps.
The track design is incredible. It lives up to the name, and the track morphs and changes as you go on, making you utilize new stratigies or methods to get to the finish line. Each vehicle style (car, boat, plane) handles exactly the way you'd expect it to, which means any time you mess up, it's always your fault.
The characters are great too. Some may have more handling, top speed, acceleration, and so on, but you can fine tune these settings with character mods that you unlock simply through playing that specific character enough. Soon you'll unlock mods that will more drastically change the way the character handles. This way if you're playing online, you'll almost always have the car stats you want, even if someone else picks your usual character.
Even the minor things, like the over-excited arcade style announcer, the wide varity of characters, and the track specific music add up to make this a great competator to Mario Kart that beats it hands down in one category: it's on the PC.
Tip: Get a gamepad for this game. It's much better with precise acceration and turning, plus the second control stick for flipping makes it much easier than a keyboard.
It's a lot of fun, that's all you need to know.

A simple MOBA concept, destroy the enemy's base before they destroy yours. Strife is made by S2 Games, the developers behind Heroes of Newerth, Savage and Strife. While S2 may have sold away Heroes of Newerth to focus on Strife, they will need to up their game a bit more. I've read multiple negative reviews about how S2 abandons their games after a while so I'll just keep a skeptical view of their products for now.
However, do try Strife as it seems that they are focusing on this at the moment.
1. Easy to Learn
There is a tutorial campaign which helps total newbies to learn how to play.
2. All Heroes Available
Having access to all the heroes from the start ensures that the game can be balanced for all players. It also gives more variety.
3. Personal Couriers/Pets
No need to buy couriers in this game. Each hero has their own pet to send items to them from the shop, just press G.
4. Storyline / Lore
There is a story for the game. While not essential, it is a plus point for the developers.
1. Gold Gain
A bit slow. I am not used to the Gold Per Minute for Strife. At 34 gold per creep, it is 33% lower than Dota.
2. Item Price
There is also the high price of items in the game, it ranges from 4000-5000 gold for relatively decent items. A Mask of Madness copy costs close to 5000 gold.
3. Long Teleport Times
While there is no need to buy a teleport scroll, it is takes quite a while to teleport.
4. Low Player Count
Too few players playing this game. There are too many ARTS/MOBAs but only 2 major players in this market, Dota and LOL.

The battle Worms are back in shape... In 3d shape :)
Worms Revolution Follows perfectly the classic gameplay from the canonicals Worms 2/Worms Armageddon, so you always have your worms team, side view, players actions are turn based and the purpose is always the same: annihilate the adversary's team XD
One of the most typical aspects of the game is obviously the arsenal for your worms, and together with the classic weapons from previous games there are some clever innovations involving physics, such as attracting-repelling magnets, jetpacks, sentry guns, Telekinesis and my favorites: water-based weapons!... Because worms DO drown... XD
I've mentioned telekinesis because now there are various Giant items around the map you can interact with, by moving them or destroying them. You can imagine what happens by blowing up a huge bottle of water, or a stinky fish?
Another good innovation is the new worm class system: beside the standard average worms you can choose 3 more classes, Heavy, Scout and Scientist, each one with their own advantages and disadvantages. Creating your own team with a setup involving a number of classes that suits your gameplay can improve your results in battle.
And finally you can customize your soldiers with dumb props. There are hats, and items for every taste, and if they're not there it's simply because they must be unlocked by playing the single player missions.
There's a single player campaign of course, split into simple battles and puzzles with "objectives". Nothing amazing, but at least they can improve the life of the game with some challenges.
The worms AI is quite the same, they keep on using bazookas and grenades (the very basic weapons) with millimetric precision even from the very edge of the terrain. So... yes the real fun and challeng is in PvP modes, both online or local.
The engine isn't the most impressive and relistic engine you can see but it does its job, and sometimes with some nice results (as with the water weapons behaviors). Sometimes the engine looks a bit demanding on resources, but I can't be sure, usually I'm too focused with my team battles XD
Fun game, very relaxing compared to HoN/Dota/LoL. I like it, its an easy game to understand and nice graphics. Its worth to test out! :)

The gameplay is fun and realistic for a military layman like me.
Charaters can die easily if you can't figure out where the enemies are in the super thick forest. Neither you, your teamates or enemies can look far. Enemies can be literaturelly meters away and neither of you are awared. This hide-and-seek-like feeling is what the game attracted me in the first place.
Meanwhile, the characters are as fragile as the VCs. A shot in the right part can be fatal, so better aviod close combats because you'll get shot easier. But there're also the old school first-aid bag for you to restore some health.
There're about 2 dozen of characters you can recruit into your 4-men team. They all have a class, a heavy gunner can't shoot accurately with a sniper rifle, even when controled by the player. Though the option's varied, you only need the certain four to cover all 8 campaigns.
Characters feature some status that can be upgraded after every mission, but the game's campaign is so short that it ends before you can notice your characters have grown.
The weapons also has quite a varity, including 20+ main weapon but merely 2 pistols and 20 items(mines and bombs, grenades, radios for air strike, disposable rockets launchers, binoculars....), all provide different experiences.
Each character can carry a main weapon, a pistol and 3 items at the beginning of a mission, more can be picked up during mission. Even though the in-game hint says the accuracy will be affected if carry too much, but it's probably not true according the actual gameplay.
The game mess up frequently when you need to control the movement of teammates cause their  navigation is totally piece of♥♥♥♥♥♥
They don't like to walk straight. When given the 'follow me' order, they run around the nearby area before they stop near you as you stop, only when given the 'move to' order can they move straight.
They get lost behind frequently, mostly being stucked somewhere. The map is full of bugs. Trees, rocks, cornors, rooms, even a plain ground can stop you or your teammate from time to time.They don't know how to get cross bridges, most of the time they stuck on it or directly jump into the river. So you better have the patient to control them individually to cross some parts of the maps with even just a few obstacles.
With that said, the command machanic is quite stright forward. You can hold Q to enable a command panel featuring fire at will, hold fire, crouch/prone/stand, move to, hold positon, follow, all of which are also binded on reasonable hotkeys, and all of the orders have their use.
Further more, the game crashes quite often. In the first half of the game it crashed dozens of times for some unknown reason (I suspect it's about not killing all enemies in the game) and there're no really solution for this. Frequent saving might work, but you still have to restart a mission to solve that sometime.
All in all, the game can make you mad some times by either crashing or bugs.The game's machanic is completed but lacks some polish, as some aspects are well delivered but missions are too short to support these contents. It feels realistic but fun to play as the difficulty is well controlled.

Let's start with the pros. The gunplay is decent. Maybe it's just because I've been playing other shooters, but the AR's and SMG's don't seem to have much weight to them, leaving them feeling weak (the high healthbars/high time-to-kill doesn't help in this case, but it does help in the balancing of weapons). The characters seem pretty interesting. The mobility and speed really add to the experience, and I quite enjoy the gameplay in a general sense. Why can't I recommend this game? Well...
I said that the characters "seem" interesting for a reason. If you do not spend any money on this game, you will not be able to experience anyone outside of the free rotation for quite some time. Even upon getting a new character, you can't use any weapons outside of the default kit unless you receive merc cards through cases, which are random, and again, behind a paywall/large credit wall. If you get a card for a merc that you don't own, you either have to only use it during free weeks, or play around 250 15-minute games to purchase that single character. Being at the top of the scoreboard gives you 250 credits per win, 100 per loss, and with every new merc costing you either 40,000 or 50,000 credits, you're going to be grinding quite a bit - with a single character, with a single gun. If you then purchase a character you think you'll like but end up not liking them, well, you better get on that 250-game grind with your first character. There's no way to test any characters without waiting weeks for the rotation to come to the one you want to try.
I realize this is a free-to-play game. I realize this. I know the devs have to earn money from their game somehow. But there are free-to-play games that still reward people for playing. This feels more like a pay-to-play game, it's just that the price tag is hidden until after you download it. At the very least, this is a pay-to-enjoy game, unless you're a big fan of grinding. On that note, I can not recommend this supposed free-to-play game.

Recently I was in the mood for some good ol' 2D platforming. So I gave this game a go.
It turned out to be a lot of fun. A relatively short game, you play as a goat that was imprisoned for witchcraft. Other inmates include sheep that are locked in various rooms. Each section of rooms has a unique theme to the puzzles.
Add to that, you have a little mouse companion that comes in handy, in a single-player co-op kinda way.
And once you beat the game, you get a second set of more challenging levels. The "All Intensive Purposes" rooms.
